transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thanks for coming in. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your daughter's delivery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm already tired of talking. I've been in this hospital for three days. Just tell me why the baby is still in the NICU.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, there was some confusion with the prenatal records during the admission process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion. That's what you always say. What does that actually mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means that some of the information didn't quite make it to the delivery team in the way it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the process. Is my daughter okay? Why is she on these antibiotics now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion this caused, but we were really busy with a few emergencies on the floor that night, and things didn't go quite right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy? You're telling me you were too busy to check a chart? My daughter is in an incubator and you're telling me you were busy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. The important thing is that she is receiving the treatment now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't do this. Every time I trust a doctor in this building, something happens. I just... I can't. I'm terrified she's going to have permanent brain damage.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we need to look at the current labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am terrified. Do you even hear me? I am sitting here shaking and you're talking about labs.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical team is monitoring her very closely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tell me exactly what happened. No more "confusion." What did you miss?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was an issue with how the prenatal status was communicated to the labour and delivery staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. Did you miss a test? Did you forget a drug?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a discrepancy in the record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're lying to me. You're not even telling me the truth. This is exactly like what happened with my back surgery. You people just hide things until we scream.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am not hiding anything. I'm just saying the system didn't alert the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is responsible? Give me a name.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a team effort in the delivery suite.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. My baby is sick because you people can't read a piece of paper. I don't know if I can even trust you to touch her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are doing everything we can now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens next? When do I know if she's actually going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on her. We'll see how she responds to the current meds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "See how she responds." That's not a plan. That's a guess. Give me a date. Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned to the progress. You'll probably get an email or a call from the attending later today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email. My daughter is in the NICU and I'm waiting for an email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to let the antibiotics work.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the Chief of Medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see if they're available, but it won't change the clinical path.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the path. I care about the fact that you won't even admit what you did.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained that there was a communication issue.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You haven't explained anything. You've used five different ways to avoid saying "we messed up."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry it feels that way, but the focus should be on the baby.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The focus is on the baby because you failed her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really think we should focus on the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What steps? You haven't given me any steps.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just continue the current protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a nightmare. I just wanted a healthy baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I have to go check on another patient now, so we'll talk more later.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation under pushback and uses rushing language to end the encounter ('I have to go check on another patient now').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'some confusion' and 'things didn't go quite right'.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system' and 'the delivery suite' rather than taking accountability.

R.justification: Resident uses only generic validation ('I understand') and repeatedly meets emotional bids with factual redirection to labs and protocols.

T.justification: No concrete plan is provided, using only placeholders such as 'stay tuned to the progress' and 'we'll see how she responds'.
